concepts.def: System software that manages hardware, files, processes and provides services to applications.
Core of the OS that manages CPU, memory and device access at the lowest level.
Running multiple processes seemingly at once by rapidly switching the CPU between them.
OS component that organises files in directories and tracks them on storage media.
Software that allows the OS to communicate with a specific piece of hardware.
Means by which the user interacts with the OS, e.g., GUI or command line.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Systems Architecture — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Systems Architecture brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Systems Architecture.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
